title: Pressure Washing in Dunnellon, FL | House Soft Wash
description: Pressure washing and soft washing in Dunnellon, FL for siding, stucco, porches, drives, and roofs. Mildew killed at the root, the right pressure per surface.
h1: Pressure Washing and Soft Washing in Dunnellon, FL
heroIntro: Mildew, algae, and pollen grow fast in a humid river town. We clean Dunnellon homes and businesses with the pressure each surface can actually take, from old wood siding to concrete drives.

questions: Is pressure washing safe for older wood siding?
How often should a Dunnellon home be washed?
Do I need a wash before painting?

body: With two rivers nearby and humidity that stays high all year, Dunnellon gives mildew and algae ideal conditions. Shaded walls, north-facing eaves, porch ceilings, and walkways under trees go green or black first. Pollen adds a yellow film each spring. Pressure washing in Dunnellon, FL restores the surface and, just as importantly, removes growth that will otherwise eat into paint and caulk. It is often the first service Dunnellon homeowners book with us.
Black streaks that come back quickly may point to something more than surface growth; see our guide to mold on siding.

Old wood siding on the historic homes downtown can be gouged or soaked by high pressure, forcing water behind boards and into the wall. For those homes, and for stucco, painted surfaces, screens, and roofs, we use a soft wash, where the cleaning agent does the work instead of the water jet; it is applied at garden-hose force, allowed to dwell, and rinsed away. Only hard flatwork like drives, sidewalks, and pool decks gets real pressure, run through a rotary cleaner so the concrete dries without stripes.
bullets: Wood siding and trim: soft wash only
Roofs: soft wash only, never high pressure
Porch floors and decks: low pressure to avoid raising the grain
Concrete drives and walks: surface cleaner at higher pressure

body: A repaint over mildew or chalk is a repaint that fails early. Before any exterior painting job in Dunnellon, the cleaning day is followed by a drying window long enough that scraping and priming start on a clean, bone-dry wall. Dry is confirmed, not assumed: in this climate wood can feel dry on the surface and still read high on a moisture meter.

Plants are wetted before cleaning solution goes on and rinsed after. Outlets, light fixtures, and door hardware are covered. Windows get a final rinse to prevent spotting. We aim runoff away from flower beds and, near the water, keep the cleaning footprint tight.

sections.h2: Porches, screens, and outdoor living areas
body: Porches are a big part of how people live in Dunnellon, and they collect grime fast. Porch ceilings grow mildew in the corners, screen enclosures trap pollen and spider webs, and painted porch floors turn slick in the shade. Each gets cleaned with the gentlest method that works: low-pressure rinses for screens, soft wash for ceilings, and careful cleaning of painted floors so the coating is not stripped in the process.

Shaded homes near the rivers often benefit from a wash every year; sunnier lots can go longer. A regular clean extends the life of the paint you already have. For the yellow spring film, read how to clean Florida pollen stains, or see our main pressure washing service.

faqs.q: Will pressure washing damage my historic home's siding?
faqs.a: Not with a soft wash. Older wood siding is cleaned at low pressure with a solution that kills growth, so the wood is not gouged or soaked.

faqs.q: Do you wash roofs in Dunnellon?
faqs.a: Yes, with a soft wash only. High pressure can damage roofing materials.

faqs.q: Can you wash my business storefront?
faqs.a: Yes. Commercial washing can be scheduled around operating hours, including early mornings or weekends.
